original.target_description: Original Experiment 2: achievement/verbal analogy performance following red versus gray color-word processing; primary full text could not be acquired within the bounded acquisition attempt.

replication.target_description: Experiment 1: Austrian upper secondary school students; number of correct verbal analogies after red-alder versus gray-alder example-item manipulation; independent-groups one-tailed t-test.

n.sample_role: Participants analyzed in the independent-groups t-test; red n = 30, gray n = 39
n.exclusions: No participant exclusions reported for this test; missing item responses scored incorrect. All 69 recruited participants are represented by t(67).
n.location: Full-text HTML, Experiment 1, Method; Results first paragraph; Table 1, present-study Experiment 1 row
n.quote: Sixty-nine students (41 female and 28 male) from two upper secondary schools (“Gymnasium”) in Austria; t(67) = 0.14

es.location: Full-text HTML, Experiment 1, Results, first paragraph (input PDF locator p. 7; HTML has no page breaks)
es.quote: t(67) = 0.14, p = .443, and an effect size close to zero, d = 0.04, 95% CI [–0.44, 0.51].

p.quote: t(67) = 0.14, p = .443, and an effect size close to zero, d = 0.04, 95% CI [–0.44, 0.51].

reported_success.location: Full-text HTML, Experiment 1, Results, final sentence
reported_success.quote: In summary, these analyses failed to support the hypothesis that reading the word red would impair analogy test performance.

notes: Replication title verified against supplied reference.
